summary: 9 changes, 45 tasks, all valid under openspec --strict. The assess-stage blocking question dissolved: UAR consumes THIS repo as a submodule (crates/prometheus-skill-system) and discovers skill.wasm beside SKILL.md there, so producing components is in-repo work and UAR picks them up by bumping its pointer. Ordering reversed from the seeded order: classify the 60 skills first (sizes everything), then harness verification, then fabric-integration, then WIT, then the reference component, then the FFI decision and bindings. The single cross-repo change (008) is last and isolated.
warnings: NEW FINDING: skills/rust/librefang-wasm-skill ships wasm templates targeting core-wasm extern "C" with a host_call import and ZERO .wit files. A guest built from them CANNOT load in UAR's component runtime. The divergence is three incompatible guest targets, not two WIT packages.
change-msp-005 must ABORT if re-running the three UAR discovery commands disagrees with what plan recorded — the ordering depends on cross-repo facts a single-repo reviewer cannot verify.
change-msp-008 requires explicit user authorisation for cross-repo writes. BLOCKED is the default on silence; no later change depends on it.

change-msp-004 enforces only the three invariants that currently hold; the WIT invariant is already violated and is quarantined in a self-shrinking allowlist that fails both on un-allowlisted violations and on allowlisted entries that have been fixed.

adversarial_review.notable: Round 1 caught that I had silently dropped the seeded Mobile FFI bindings goal (restored as change-msp-009). Round 2 caught that my fix for round 1's CI paradox over-corrected into an audit-only check that no longer met goal 2's 'enforced'. A planner correcting its own plan introduced a new defect while fixing the old one.
